[text-20] heading "Method"
[text-21] list item "Step 1 Put 100g plain flour, 2 large eggs, 300ml milk, 1 tbsp sunflower or vegetable oil and a pinch of salt into a bowl or large jug, then whisk to a smooth batter. This should be similar in consistency to single cream."
[text-22] list item "Step 2 Set aside for 30 mins to rest if you have time, or start cooking straight away."
[text-23] list item "Step 3 Set a medium frying pan or crêpe pan over a medium heat and carefully wipe it with some oiled kitchen paper."
[text-24] list item "Step 4 When hot, cook your pancakes for 1 min on each side until golden, using around half a ladleful of batter per pancake. Keep them warm in a low oven as you make the rest."
[text-25] list item "Step 5 Serve with lemon wedges and caster sugar, or your favourite filling. Once cold, you can layer the pancakes between baking parchment, then wrap in cling film and freeze for up to two months."
[text-26] heading "Frequently asked questions"
[text-27] heading "What is the best pan to make these pancakes?"
[text-28] "For crêpes, you can use a non-stick frying pan, if you have one with sloped sides, that's good for sliding them out once cooked. A seasoned cast iron pan will work well for both American style and crêpes. Avoid stainless steel frying pans, as if you are not familiar cooking in them, the risk of stic"
[text-29] heading "What should I do if the batter seems too thin/runny?"
[text-30] "This classic pancake batter is supposed to be thin, like the consistency of single cream. However, if you’re looking for a slightly thicker crêpe batter then try our classic crêpes. For a much thicker and fluffy consistency, make our American pancakes recipe."
[text-31] heading "How much batter should I use per pancake?"
[text-32] "For crêpes, use a ladle and pour enough into the pan, swirling it so that it just coats the bottom, if you are using a large pan, you can double the recipe. To make 12 crêpes as above, you will want to use a 18cm frying pan, measured over the base. For American-style use 2-3 tbsp of batter per panca"
[text-33] heading "My pancakes are not cooking in the middle"
[text-34] "You may be using too much batter for each pancake. Aim for a thin layer on the bottom of the pan to ensure it cooks evenly."
[text-35] heading "My batter is quite lumpy, how can I make it smoother?"
[text-36] "Prevent lumps forming by slowly whisking the liquid into the flour. If you do get some lumps, whizz it in a food processor."
[text-37] "Improve your pancake skills with our how to make pancakes video and our how to flip a pancake video."
[text-38] "Recipe from Good Food magazine, February 2013"

extent.instructions: Only when the action scrolls the page or a scrolling part of it: how far? Choose words when the words give a number of screens or pages; screen when they say nothing of how far. Ignored for every other action.

options.words: as many screens as the number the words carry
options.little: a little: a third of a screen
options.screen: one screen, as Page Down does
options.end: all the way: to the bottom, or to the top going up

amount.instructions: Only when the action skips forward or back in a video or audio, changes its volume or speed, or changes an app number (a setting's amount, the panel's width): how far? For a skip, choose words when the words say how far — a number of seconds, or of minutes; otherwise the share of its length the words mean. For a volume, a speed or an app number, choose to when the words carry the level, else up or down and how far. Ignored for every other action.

options.words: as far as the words say: the number they carry, in seconds, or in minutes when they say minutes
options.moment: a moment: a hundredth of its length
options.little: a little: a twentieth of its length
options.chunk: a chunk: a tenth of its length
options.lot: a lot: a quarter of its length
options.end: all the way: to the end, or back to the start
options.to: the volume, speed or app number to the number the words carry
options.up-little: the volume, speed or app number up a little
options.up-step: the volume, speed or app number up a step
options.up-lot: the volume, speed or app number up a lot
options.up-all: the volume, speed or app number up as far as it goes
options.down-little: the volume, speed or app number down a little
options.down-step: the volume, speed or app number down a step
options.down-lot: the volume, speed or app number down a lot
options.down-all: the volume, speed or app number down as far as it goes
